entries.rationale: Foundry already reaches the setting store through ProjectSettings::get_singleton() (fs_parser.cpp:136), which is exactly godot-cpp's shape.
non_mappings: core's GLOBAL_GET/GLOBAL_DEF macros appear nowhere in godot-cpp; ported code must spell ProjectSettings::get_singleton()->get_setting_with_override() (gen/include/godot_cpp/classes/project_settings.hpp:57,62).

entries.rationale: The include is vestigial: no CoreConstants symbol appears anywhere in the port set. The port drops the include rather than inventing a mapping for a dependency that is not real.

Every ERR_* macro the port set uses is spelled identically in godot-cpp, so the thin macro shim predicted by docs/foundry-reuse-plan.md section 3 would be a rename-free wrapper and is declined. The seam instead #errors when a required macro is undefined, so a godot-cpp bump that drops one is a compile error rather than a silent no-op.
non_mappings: core's ERR_FAIL_* route through _err_print_error with a Godot Error code; godot-cpp's route through the GDExtension print interface. Message text and exit behaviour are not byte-identical, so diagnostics compared by a corpus must not come from these macros.

entries.rationale: godot-cpp has no Compression class, but it does have the same codec: PackedByteArray::compress/decompress take a mode enumerator that FileAccess spells as COMPRESSION_ZSTD. The shim is a rename over exactly that, and it keeps core's contract that decompression is told the expected size up front rather than growing a buffer.
non_mappings: core's Compression::decompress returns the decompressed length; godot-cpp's returns an empty array on failure, which is indistinguishable from decompressing to nothing. The caller compares the result size against the size its own header recorded, so a truncated or corrupt block is a data error rather than a short read.

entries.rationale: Absent from godot-cpp, and the four functions the tokenizer buffer uses split into two cases. encode_uint32/decode_uint32 are byte-order definitions -- core writes a uint32 little-endian, byte by byte -- so reimplementing them is exact rather than approximate. encode_variant/decode_variant reach the same serializer through UtilityFunctions::var_to_bytes/bytes_to_var, which is core's encode_variant with p_full_objects = false: the mode the buffer already asked for, because a constant is never an object.
non_mappings: core's decode_variant reports how many bytes one value consumed through an r_len out-parameter; UtilityFunctions::bytes_to_var does not, and the seam does not invent one. BSTokenizerBuffer length-prefixes each pooled constant instead, so the framing a reader needs is written down rather than guessed.

core's encode_variant can be called with a null buffer to size an encoding before writing it; godot-cpp's always allocates. The buffer writer appends the encoded block directly, so the sizing pass has no consumer here.

core's ResourceLoader::load is a static member (fs_parser.cpp:7488); godot-cpp's is an instance method on the singleton (gen/include/godot_cpp/classes/resource_loader.hpp:72,77) and drops core's trailing Error out-parameter. Call sites change, so this is a header mapping, not a call-compatible one.

entries.rationale: ResourceUID::ensure_path is a static member in both trees (godot-cpp at gen/include/godot_cpp/classes/resource_uid.hpp:65), so the one call site at fs_parser.cpp:1150 ports unchanged.
core reaches the Math:: free functions transitively through core/math/math_funcs.h; godot-cpp keeps them in core/math.hpp, so the seam includes both to preserve the single include.
core declares RefCounted and Ref<T> in one header; godot-cpp splits Ref<T> into classes/ref.hpp, so the seam includes both.
The port set only needs Script (Ref<Script>, Script::get_class_static()); core declares it alongside ScriptLanguage in one header, godot-cpp splits them.
non_mappings: ScriptInstance has no godot-cpp equivalent -- gen/include/godot_cpp/classes/ holds script.hpp, script_language.hpp, script_extension.hpp and script_language_extension.hpp and nothing else -- so the extension implements ScriptInstanceExtension instead.
Foundry's trait virtuals on ScriptLanguage are not in stock Godot (D5); BaristaScript owns its own trait registry.
core/object/script_function_state.h is engine-internal and is not reachable from a GDExtension; coroutines get their own suspended-frame object.

entries.rationale: Same classification predicates over char32_t, relocated from core/string to godot_cpp/variant.

Absent from godot-cpp. Guarding it out was rejected: it would delete FSParser::TreePrinter, the parser's only AST dump. Vendoring Godot's MIT original was rejected on inspection rather than on principle: as_string() builds its result with String::resize_uninitialized, which godot-cpp's String does not have (it exposes resize, ptr and ptrw at gen/include/godot_cpp/variant/string.hpp:417,496,497, but no uninitialized resize), so the vendored copy would need editing -- and an edited vendor loses the upstream diffability that is vendoring's only advantage. The seam therefore reimplements the public API over String concatenation: the same observable behaviour, including the empty-append and empty-result rules, with a different cost profile. That is a shim, not an alias to a near-miss type.

The StringName type maps exactly, but SNAME -- used 39 times in fs_parser.cpp -- is a core macro with no godot-cpp counterpart. The seam supplies it with core's own semantics: a function-local static StringName constructed on first use.

non_mappings: godot-cpp's String is an opaque byte array dispatched through _method_bindings into the GDExtension interface, so it has no ptrw/resize/copy_from_unchecked and does not work without a loaded Godot runtime. No ported frontend code can be exercised from a standalone C++ test binary.

entries.rationale: Foundry's own addition. D1 gives BaristaScript one integer type, so the numeric tower is deleted rather than ported. The seam poisons the identifier so a surviving reference is a compile error naming the decision, never a stub that lets the tower creep back.

non_mappings: core/variant/container_type_validate.h, which Foundry extended with numeric_type and type_arguments, has no godot-cpp equivalent and is not mapped here; BaristaScript owns its own type descriptor (D2).

entries.rationale: Reached only under TOOLS_ENABLED, for editor colour and comment settings that belong to the editor-integration milestone. A GDExtension reaches editor settings through EditorInterface, not this header, so the seam maps nothing and the port drops the guarded block.
Only the RPCMode enumerators are used (fs_parser.cpp:8127, :8148); godot-cpp exposes them on the same class.

Reached only under DEBUG_ENABLED, for the TextServer::FEATURE_UNICODE_SECURITY confusable check (fs_tokenizer.cpp:672, fs_parser.cpp:4898). The check is a warning aid, not a parse decision, and pulling the whole TextServer binding into every ported translation unit to keep it is not worth it in M1. Recorded as an explicit omission so the warning milestone can reinstate it deliberately.
